title: How can I determine whether there is a gas leak in my gas cooker?
desc: Keep an eye out for signs such as bubbles in soapy water applied to connections, audible hissing noises, or a distinct gas smell.

title: Is the yellow flame on my gas cooker normal?
desc: Flames that are yellow or irregular can be a sign of combustion problems, such as an unclean burner. Contact a professional if you face this problem.

title: If the igniter on my gas cooker keeps clicking, what should I do?
desc: A malfunctioning igniter or moisture may be to blame for this. Make sure the area is clean and dry; if the problem continues, you might need to hire a professional repairman.

title: Why won't my gas stove light up?
desc: Problems with the burner, igniter, or gas supply could be the cause. Look for obvious obstacles, and if the issue continues, get help from a professional.

title: How frequently should my gas cooker be serviced?
desc: To guarantee safe and effective operation, every six months maintenance is advised. Frequent inspections help prolong the appliance's life and reduce possible problems.
